note: Worldwide context and non-Iowa examples only. None of these records activates a crop trait, field suitability test, or rotation rule.

records.title: Historical climate at a world coordinate
records.claim: NASA POWER's Daily API supplies analysis-ready daily meteorological time series for a requested point. FieldShift uses it for historical temperature and precipitation context.
records.applicability: Only dates and variables returned with valid values for the selected coordinate and period.
records.limitations: The grid is not a field weather station; resolution varies by source variable. Missing days and differences from local conditions must remain visible. This is not a seasonal forecast.

records.title: Satellite precipitation context
records.claim: NASA GPM IMERG combines satellite observations into half-hourly precipitation estimates over most of Earth.
records.geography: Near-global product; coverage and inputs vary by latitude and run
records.applicability: Historical precipitation context only where the exact service returns complete, valid samples.
records.limitations: A satellite-grid estimate is not a field rain gauge or soil-moisture measurement. FieldShift's tested service has returned incomplete days, so no daily total is shown unless all required intervals are valid.

records.title: Global mapped soil: a candidate, not an active lookup
records.claim: ISRIC offers global SoilGrids maps, but reports that its beta REST API is temporarily paused; WCS and WebDAV remain alternative access routes.
records.applicability: Researching a future worldwide soil layer; not currently used for a field result in FieldShift.
records.limitations: No global soil result is integrated or validated here. Modeled grid values would not replace local soil sampling, and API availability can change.

records.title: Crop names are not growing advice
records.claim: GBIF's species service supports worldwide plant-name lookup, while FAO Ecocrop is a broader library of crop descriptors.
records.applicability: Discovering names and external reference material; no crop is admitted to a local rotation comparison from these sources alone.
records.limitations: GBIF is taxonomy, not a crop-only suitability database. FAO says the original Ecocrop database was discontinued around 2015. Neither provides current, field-validated advice for the selected location.

records.title: Diversification is a design question, not a universal recipe
records.claim: FAO describes crop rotations with different roots and species as a way to explore soil layers, nutrient cycling, and crop-specific pest and disease breaks.
records.applicability: A question to investigate when considering locally feasible crops, seasons, residue, water, markets, and management.
records.limitations: This guidance does not identify the best sequence, guarantee a benefit, or quantify an effect for any field. Outcomes depend on local conditions and the whole management system.

records.title: Rotation outcomes differ across continents and crop sequences
records.claim: A 2025 meta-analysis combined 3,663 paired field-trial yield observations from 738 experiments across six continents. It found varied outcomes by region and crop sequence, including some transitions with unfavorable yield, nutrition, or revenue tradeoffs.
records.geography: Field trials across six continents; uneven coverage by crop and region
records.applicability: Research context for asking which crop sequence, comparison crop, input costs, and local conditions matter before using a rotation result.
records.limitations: A pooled average is not a prediction for a selected field. The study reports gross revenue, not profit, because input-cost data were insufficient; some crop combinations showed no significant gain or negative tradeoffs.

records.title: North China Plain: a six-year field experiment
records.claim: A six-year North China Plain experiment compared wheat–maize double-cropping with diversified systems including legumes and cash crops, and reported improvements in several measured production, emissions, and soil-health outcomes.
records.applicability: Evidence from the studied crops, site, management, and 2016–2022 period; an example of how a regional rotation can be evaluated.
records.limitations: Study findings and modeled regional extrapolations cannot be transferred as predicted yield, carbon, emissions, or income benefits for another field. The original study needs local comparison and agronomist review before a rule is created.

records.title: Burkina Faso: adaptation with farmers
records.claim: An FAO report describes farmer-led testing of conservation-agriculture and crop-diversification practices in five communities in south-western Burkina Faso.
records.applicability: A process example for local evaluation of crop-livestock systems, not a validated crop sequence for the app.
records.limitations: This is a 2010 case report, not a controlled global effect estimate. Its cropping system, climate, and available resources differ from other regions.
